item.title: [−1] Black Sea war puts India's food security at risk as El Niño threatens the rabi season
item.description:
Black Sea shipping attacks threaten edible oil, grain and fertiliser supply. India cut its 2026–27 foodgrain target, and Karnataka declared 265 of 358 talukas drought-hit. Fertiliser stocks are 38% higher at 17.01 million tonnes. Ongoing.

FMCG & consumer: mild headwind (−1) — Edible oil and grain costs

Why it matters: Supply risks and a weak rabi crop raise food and edible oil prices, feeding inflation, while ample fertiliser stocks soften the hit to farm output.

Market gauges: Inflation outlook −1, Growth outlook −1

Confidence: low · horizon: months
